what: AI review, 2026-11-21, of how the sixth rehearsal of the full-run driver was written up before it was committed: the new section of records/cloud/full-rehearsals/README.md, the replay estimate rebuilt on that run (analysis/replay_cost.py and records/cloud/replay_cost.json), section 8.6 of docs/cloud-notes.md on the spending cap, a change to the launcher's cap test, and every statement elsewhere that the day's events had made stale. Five reviewers, one area each (the figures, the run against the driver's code, the cost script, the cap section, stale statements), all read-only; then a sceptic for each, who tried to refute every finding and added what the reviewer had missed. Several findings are one fault seen from two or three areas. A rehearsal tests the driver; nothing here is evidence about the proof.
the_finding_that_mattered_most: The first write-up said the rehearsal's checks cost 13 percent more than the fitted line gives, and that the replay of the whole tree would take 9.6 hours if that held. That set two different measures against each other: throughput in a trial window (jobs times the seconds between the first and last result, per module) against a line whose first point is the mean of the seconds recorded per check in another run's main pass. Like for like, trial against trial, the run is 4 to 8 percent above the line's prediction (8.8 to 9.1 hours), which is within what two windows of one run differ by. The script now compares only like with like and reports how far the line moves with the choice of its first point; the documents were corrected.
what_was_done: analysis/replay_cost.py: the ratio of unlike measures removed; the trial at 32 of the sixth rehearsal is set against the trial at 32 of the third, as throughput and as seconds per check, with the ratio the fit predicts beside them; each window now reports how many checks were in flight; the line is also given with its first point taken from the third rehearsal's trial; results recorded as 'holding modules beneath' are counted; the module's own file is counted on the search path; the docstring says which measure is which and how long the script takes.

Documents: '13 percent' and '9.6 hours' replaced everywhere by the like-for-like figures; the statement that the links cost 'under a tenth of a second' withdrawn (they were not timed, and the difference it rested on is inside the one-second resolution of the record); the main pass of 635 modules explained (26 workers, 21 checks in flight) and no longer compared with anything.

The sixth run's section: the real half-written file is attributed to the second restart test, not the time box; the driver's own trial rate of 7.13 a second is given beside the 6.9 measured between first and last result; the deep walk is said to be in probe mode and on which lemma; the second replay's exit status 3 is explained; 'made and removed' for the links reduced to what the records show; the zone is given with its source.

Section 8.6: the two rows that came from the ninth agent alone are marked as unchecked; every Spot cap is said to need a lower ledger rate; the single Spot attempt's time limit is compared with the guest's stop, an hour inside it, not with the deletion time; its spend is given at the ledger rate with its rehearsal; the resumable Spot row says that stopping a machine takes spend outside the cap; the 128 GB row says the axiom check may time out; the cheaper-family row gives its cap, its guessed speed and its deadline risk; the Mac row gives the build's full range, the INCONCLUSIVE outcome and the open-files limit; the review is placed before the rehearsal's result was known and the recomputation for 9.86 USD is stated; 'more than the bill' corrected to 'more than the list price of the machine time'; Spot prices, capacity and the preemptible-quota trap added.

verdicts.title: The '13 percent' excess and the 9.6 hours compare unlike measures
verdicts.why: Reproduced from the two c3_results.tsv.gz files using the phases.tsv windows. Fit point 1 (replay_cost.json points[0], 4.36) is the mean of recorded seconds over the third rehearsal's 745 main-pass checks (analysis/replay_cost.py, window 'check:N=32'). The 4.65 it is compared with is job-seconds (32 x span / n) from the sixth run's trial at 32, which covered 592 modules, not 1,662. Measured the same way, the third rehearsal's own trial at 32 gives 4.571 job-s and 4.659 recorded, both above its fitted 4.36. Comparing trial with trial and moving the fit to 10,462 files predicts about 4.32 job-s or 4.40 recorded for the sixth run, against 4.65 and 4.56 measured: about 8 and 4 percent over. In the main pass the sixth run records 4.09 against 4.11, about 0. The README's own sentence that the third rehearsal 'measured 4.7 in the same trial' (its recorded mean, 4.66), set against 4.65 job-s, is a third mixed comparison. 'Costs nothing extra for shallow modules' cannot sit beside a 13 percent excess.
verdicts.better_fix: The reviewer's fix is right, but the range is better given as 'about 4 to 8 percent in the trial, measured like for like, and about 0 in the main pass'. 13 percent is an artefact of the mixed measures, so it should not stay as the top of the range. Give 9.6 h only as 'an upper reading', or drop it. In CLAIMS M8 and performance-notes, say that the 4.65 is from the 592 checks of the trial.

verdicts.title: 'Under a tenth of a second' for the links was not measured
verdicts.why: rhv_tools.py closure-worker makes the links (os.link) before it calls kernel_check_one.sh, and that script's timer runs from t0 at line 79 to t1 at line 120, so recorded seconds leave the links out. The only place a link cost can show is the gap between job-seconds and recorded seconds: 4.649 - 4.561 = 0.09. In the third rehearsal, which made no links, the same gap is 4.571 - 4.659 = -0.09. Both measures have one-second resolution. So the figure sits inside the noise and is not a measurement.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer says. Or the shorter: 'The links were not timed; their cost is too small to see at the one-second resolution of the record.'

verdicts.title: Caps of 50, 46 to 48 and 56 to 58 in the 8.6 table need a lower ledger rate, which the table does not say
verdicts.why: pilot_local.sh line 41 sets RATE from GCP_RATE_USD_PER_HOUR with a default of 2.00, and line 152 computes WORST = RATE x (MAXRUN+120)/3600 + 0.01. At 2.00, a 33 to 35 h limit gives a worst case of 66 to 70, and with 9.86 spent that needs a cap of 76 to 80, not 50. The record assumes the rate is set near the Spot price. missing_options[1] (F) has 'At RATE 1.15 ... 1.12', options[2] (C) has 'RATE 0.86 / 0.90', missing_options[2] (G) has 'RATE up to ... 0.91', and options[1] (B) has 1.10. The 'What it takes' cells name the Spot flag but not the rate.
verdicts.better_fix: A note under the table is enough: 'Each Spot cap assumes GCP_RATE_USD_PER_HOUR in config.env lowered to about the Spot rate (1.10 to 1.15 for n4d-highmem-32, 0.86 to 0.90 for n4d-standard-32); at the default 2.00 none of them fits 50.'

Every phase ran in the order the code sets and did what the code intends.

The odd values in facts.json all follow from the code:
- **`every_compiled_module_passed_by_leanchecker` is false.** 1,663 .olean files exist but one (GelfandPsB) has no .hash file. `replay_state` marks it `no_stamp`, so it is never planned and never counted. Separately, 173,524 sources were never compiled, so `structure_ok` is false.
- **`passes_after_the_trials` is 1.** `C3_PASSES=1` is set before the main pass. The retry loop never started because `leanchecker_still_to_check` was 0, since the no-stamp module is excluded from that count.
- **`main_pass_seconds_allowed` is 2101.** It is not tied to the trial estimate. It is `left - FINAL_RESERVE` at +899 s: deadline 55 min = 3,300 s, so 2,401 s left, minus the rehearsal's reserve of 300.
- **The trial rate is 7.13.** That is 428 results timed between t+30 (the warm-up is a third of the 90 s trial) and the trial's end, divided by `TRIAL_SECS - warm` = 60.
- **The second replay's exit status is 3.** For `rhv-replay` the script adds `--require-complete`, and `complete_by` is false because `structure_ok` is false. The main pass's status 3 comes from `--require-c3` for the same reason.
- **The main pass took 129 s against 90 expected.** 635 modules made 26 batches of 25, so only 26 of 32 slots ever worked: concurrency from the results file was 25 to 26 throughout, then about 30 s of tail at 9, 1 and 0.5. The pass also includes planning, the summary and root's `c3_summary`. Time inside `leanchecker` was lower than in the trial (4.1 s against 4.5 s per check).

The one scale defect: with 25 modules per batch, a retry pass over a few dozen killed modules runs in 2 or 3 serial processes, not the 8 it is given. The README section has one claim the records contradict (which kill left the real half-written file), one fact missing from every file in the run directory (the zone), a rate that does not match the facts.json figure, and a deep-walk row that leaves out "probe".

findings.what_is_wrong: The plan is cut into batches of 25 and each batch is one serial worker. When a pass has fewer than JOBS*25 modules, it gets ceil(N/25) workers, not JOBS. review.area_summary:
I checked analysis/replay_cost.py (its diff and the whole script) and its output. Running it with --driver-run 20261120-235539 --closure-run 20261121-113516 and no --out gives output identical to records/cloud/replay_cost.json apart from made_utc (18:04:39Z in the file, 18:09:51Z from my run). I compared the result after sorting keys and removing made_utc, and I also diffed the raw files. The arithmetic is right: fixed 2.6028, per_file 0.0001435, fit(9.5) = 4.107, closure_dir = 5.567 s (8.47 h), 4.65/4.107 = 1.132, 5.567 x 1.132 = 6.3 s (9.6 h).

The finding that matters is the comparison, not the code. The line's first point (4.36) is the mean time inside leanchecker per check, taken over the third rehearsal's MAIN pass. That pass had 745 modules, which at 25 per worker is 30 workers, so under the new code's own rule it would not count as "all_jobs_busy". The 4.65 is a different quantity: 32 x span / n, a throughput figure from the sixth rehearsal's TRIAL.

Comparing like with like from both runs' c3_results.tsv.gz and phases.tsv:
- Trial at 32 at a time: run 3 (whole library, 12,244 files) gives 4.57 job-s and 4.66 mean seconds inside leanchecker. Run 6 (closure directories, about 10,462 files) gives 4.65 and 4.56.
- Main pass, mean seconds inside leanchecker: run 3 gives 4.36. Run 6 gives 4.09, where the fit gives 4.107 (ratio 1.00).

So the third rehearsal's own trial sits 5 to 7 percent above the line at its own search-path size. Measured against like windows, the sixth run exceeds the projection by 0 to 8 percent (8.4 to 9.1 h), not 13 percent (9.6 h). The fit predicts the shorter search path saves only 0.25 s (6 percent) at this size, which is about the noise between windows. So the rehearsal neither confirms nor refutes the per-file term that drives 8.5 h against 46 h.

Smaller issues:
- The closure count leaves out the module's own file, which closure-worker does link (off by one, negligible).
- Rows marked "...-holding-modules-beneath" are left out, which is harmless here.
- The docstring's "about ten" seconds is wrong.
- The JSON note says "import 10 others" where the documents say 9.
